description: Invented demo negotiation for npm run simulate (not from the brief, not from the eval dataset). delay_ms in [1000,3000].

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Thanks for joining. The proposal covers 80 analyst seats with onboarding included, starting next month.

turns.speaker: counterpart
turns.text: Appreciate it. The platform looks solid, but the price is well above what finance approved for this year.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Understood. Which part of the budget gap matters most to you, the licence fee or the onboarding cost?

turns.speaker: counterpart
turns.text: Mostly the licence fee. We have a quote from another vendor that comes in about twenty percent lower.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Oh, okay. Sorry, we can definitely drop the price by twenty percent, whatever works for you.

turns.speaker: counterpart
turns.text: Great. And we will need the security review done by legal before we can say anything about a start date.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Can we put a date on the legal review? Our onboarding team needs two weeks of notice.

turns.speaker: counterpart
turns.text: It is hard to say. Legal has a long queue, so let us just see how things go over the next few weeks.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: If the review slips past the end of the month, the discount we discussed will not be available anymore.

turns.speaker: counterpart
turns.text: Then we are done here. Either the discount holds without conditions or we sign with the other vendor today.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I hear you. Let us keep the discount and agree a named legal contact plus a review date this week.

turns.speaker: counterpart
turns.text: Fair enough. Maria from our legal team will confirm the review date with you by Thursday.
